RagShortTexts: The ruling elite of Armenia comprised ancient aristocratic houses and military dynasties competing for feudal land and fiscal control.
Domestic politics were profoundly steered by court intrigues and noble factions resisting excessive central centralization.
Intricate matrimonial alliances and blood feuds permeated the nobility, ensuring that disputed successions frequently sparked nationwide crises.

Variants.Content: Within the opulent halls and sprawling feudal estates of Armenia, the balance of domestic power remained in perilous equilibrium. Ancient lineages commanded vast agricultural latifundia, hereditary warrior retinues, and lucrative trade monopolies, acting simultaneously as imperial cornerstones and covert rivals to the throne. Court assemblies seethed with venomous factionalism, pitting entrenched senatorial aristocrats against battle-hardened military commanders who demanded greater political dominance. Behind tapestried corridors, clandestine poisonings, forged wills, and intercepted treaties dictated political ascendancy. Lesser vassals maneuvered cautiously between dominant magnates, ready to shift allegiance whenever the central authority showed signs of exhaustion or military defeat.

Stone-hall guards keep watch while the family argues over who inherits the grain estates. A servant carrying the wine jug hears the lord's brother promise a sum the household cannot pay. The guards keep their voices low and their hands near their shields, aware that a noble quarrel can turn into a feud between villages.

The Arsacid court has summoned the great houses to the capital, and your rival has already sent gifts to the king's chamberlain. Send your most trusted cousin to the eastern estates to gather the village headmen's oaths, carrying a sealed letter only as far as the first fortress. Name your rival in no document, since royal clerks copy every word they can reach.
